Ἀσάφ.long: Asa, son of Abijah and father of Jehoshaphat, king of Judah about 900 B.C. for 41 years.
Ἀσάφ.as:
Ἀσάφ, ὁ indecl.
(Heb. אָסַף),
Asaph, an obvious error for Ἀσά, found in the best texts, and adopted by LTTr. and WH, R, mg.: Mt 1:7, 8.†

ἀστήρ.sd: a star (as strown over the sky), literally or figuratively
ἀστήρ.der: probably from the base of G4766 (στρώννυμι);
ἀστήρ.as:
ἀστήρ, -έρος, ὁ,
[in LXX chiefly for כּוֹכָב;]
a star: Mt 2:2, 7, 9, 10, Mk 13:25, I Co 15:41, Re 6:138:10, 11, 129:112:1, 4; metaph., ὁ ἀ. ὁ πρωϊνόςRe 2:2822:16; ἀ. πλαῆται, Ju 13; ἀ. ἑπτά, symbolizing the angels of the seven churches, Re 1:16, 202:13:1 (cf. ἄστρον, and v. DCG, ii, 674 f.; MM, s.v.).†

ἄσβεστος.der: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a derivative of G4570 (σβέννυμι);
ἄσβεστος.as:
ἄ-σβεστος, -ον
(< σβέννυμι), [in LXX for נפחלֹא, Jb 20:26א3 A (ἄκαυστον, א2 B)*;]
unquenched, unquenchable: πῦρ, Mt 3:12, Mk 9:43, Lk 3:17.†

ἀσπάζομαι.g: I greet, salute, pay my respects to
ἀσπάζομαι.long: I greet, salute, pay my respects to, welcome.
ἀσπάζομαι.sd: to enfold in the arms, i.e. (by implication) to salute, (figuratively) to welcome
ἀσπάζομαι.der: from G1 (Α) (as a particle of union) and a presumed form of G4685 (σπάω);
ἀσπάζομαι.as:
ἀσπάζομαι depon.,
[in LXX: Ez 18:7, Jg 18:15 (לְשָׁלוֹםשָׁאַל), Es 5:2, I Mac 7:29, al.;]
to welcome, greet, salute: c. acc. pers., Mt 5:47, Mk 9:15, Ac 21:7, al.; id. seq. ἐν φιλήματι, Ro 16:16, I Co 16:20, II Co 13:12, I Th 5:26, I Pe 5:14; τ. ἐκκλησίαν (Deiss., BS, 257), Ac 18:22; as term. tech. for conveying greetings at the end of a letter (MM, s.v.), used by an amanuensis (Milligan, NTD, 23), Ro 16:22 (on the aoristic pres., here and elsewhere, v. M, Pr., 119; Bl., § 56, 4); κατήντησαν . . . ἀσπασάμενοι (on this constr., v. Bl., § 58, 4; M, Pr., 132, 238), Ac 25:13 (cf. ἀπ-ασπάζομαι).†

ἀσθένεια.long: want of strength, weakness, illness, suffering, calamity, frailty.
ἀσθένεια.sd: feebleness (of mind or body); by implication, malady; morally, frailty
ἀσθένεια.as:
ἀσθένεια, -ας, ἡ
(< ἀσθενής), [in LXX for כּשׁל, etc.;]
weakness, frailty, sickness: Lk 13:11, 12, Jo 11:4, Ac 28:9, Ro 6:198:26, II Co 11:3013:4, Ga 4:13 (MM, s.v.), He 5:27:2811:34; ἐν ἀ., Jo 5:5, I Co 2:315:43, II Co 12:9; pl., Mt 8:17, Lk 5:158:2, II Co 12:512:9, 10, I Ti 5:23, He 4:15.†
SYN.: μαλακία, νόσος (v. DB, iii, 323a).

ἀσκός.sd: a leathern (or skin) bag used as a bottle
ἀσκός.as:
ἀσκός, -οῦ, ὁ,
[in LXX for חֵמֶת, נֹאד, נֵבֶל;]
a leather bottle, wine-skin: Mt 9:17, Mk 2:22, Lk 5:37, 38.†

ἀσθενέω.long: I am weak (physically: then morally), I am sick.
ἀσθενέω.kj: be diseased, impotent folk (man), (be) sick, (be, be made) weak
ἀσθενέω.as:
ἀσθενέω, -ῶ
(< ἀσθενής), [in LXX chiefly for כּשׁל;]
to be weak, feeble: Ac 20:35, Ro 8:3, II Co 11:2112:1013:4, 9; c. dat., πίστει (Cremer, 527), Ro 4:1914:1; same implied, Ro 14:2, 21, I Co 8:11, 12, II Co 11:29; εἰς, II Co 13:3. Specif., of bodily debility, to be sick: Mt 25:36, 39, Lk 4:40, Jo 4:465:3, 7, 1311:1-3, 6, Ac 9:37, Phl 2:26, 27, II Ti 4:20, Ja 5:14; οἱ ἀσθενοῦντες, the sick: Mt 10:8 (MM, s.v.), Mk 6:56, Lk 9:2, Ac 19:12.†

ἀσσάριον.long: a small coin equal to the tenth part of a drachma.
ἀσσάριον.sd: an assarius or as, a Roman coin
ἀσσάριον.as:
*† ἀσσάριον, -ον, τό
(dim. of Lat. as),
an assarion, a farthing, one-tenth of a drachma: Mt 10:29, Lk 12:6 (MM, s.v.; DB, iii, 428; DCG, ii, 200).†

ἀσύνετος.long: unintelligent, without wisdom, unwise, undiscerning (implying probably moral defect).
ἀσύνετος.der: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and G4908 (συνετός);
ἀσύνετος.as:
ἀ-σύνετος, -ον
[in LXX: De 32:21 (נָבָל), Jb 13:2 (נפל), Ps 91 (92):6 (כְּסִיל), Ps 75 (76):5, Wi2, Si6*;]
without understanding or discernment: Mt 15:16, Mk 7:18 (Swete, in l.), Ro 1:21, 3110:19 (for an ex. of its use in the moral sense, v. MM, s.v.).†

ἀσπασμός.sd: a greeting (in person or by letter)
ἀσπασμός.as:
* ἀσπασμός, -οῦ, ὁ
(< ἀσπάζομαι),
a salutation (so always in RV), greeting: oral, Mt 23:7, Mk 12:38, Lk 1:29, 41, 4411:4320:46; written, I Co 16:21, Col 4:18, II Th 3:17.†

ἀστραπή.g: a flash of lightning, brightness, luster
ἀστραπή.long: a flash of lightning, brightness, luster.
ἀστραπή.as:
ἀστραπή, -ῆς, ἡ,
[in LXX for בָּרָק;]
lightning: Mt 24:2728:3, Lk 10:1817:24; pl., Re 4:58:511:1916:18; of a lamp, shining brightness, Lk 11:36.†

ἀσθενής.long: (lit: not strong), (a) weak (physically, or morally), (b) infirm, sick.
ἀσθενής.sd: strengthless (in various applications, literal, figurative and moral)
ἀσθενής.kj: more feeble, impotent, sick, without strength, weak(-er, -ness, thing)
ἀσθενής.der: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and the base of G4599 (σθενόω);
ἀσθενής.as:
* ἀσθενής, -ές
(< ἀ- neg., σθένος, strength), [in LXX for עָנִי, etc.;]
without strength, weak, feeble: I Co 1:274:1012:22, II Co 10:10, Ga 4:9, I Th 5:14, He 7:18, I Pe 3:7. Rhetorically, τό ἀ. τ. θεοῦ, God's action of apparent weakness: I Co 1:25; of bodily debility, sick, sickly: Mt 25:39 (Rec.) Mt 25:43, 44, Lk 9:2 (Rec.) 10:9, Ac 4:95:15, 16 In moral and spiritual sense (MM, s.v.; Cremer, 526), Mt 26:41, Mk 14:38, Ro 5:6, I Co 8:7, 8:9, 109:2211:30.†

ἀσφαλίζω.as:
† ἀσφαλίζω
(< ἀσφαλής), [in LXX: Ne 3:15 (חזק hi.), Is 41:10 (תּמךְ), Wi 4:1710:1213:15*;]
to make firm, secure: mid., Mt 27:65, 66, Ac 16:24; pass., Mt 27:64 (MM, s.v.).†

ἀσέλγεια.long: (outrageous conduct, conduct shocking to public decency, a wanton violence), wantonness, lewdness.
ἀσέλγεια.der: from a compound of G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a presumed (of uncertain derivation, but apparently meaning continent);
ἀσέλγεια.as:
** ἀσέλγεια, -ας, ἡ
(< ἀσελγής, licentious; v. MM, s.v.), [in LXX: Wi 14:26, III Mac 2:26*;]
licentiousness, wantonness, excess: Mk 7:22, Ro 13:13, II Co 12:21, Ga 5:19 (Lft., in l.), Eph 4:19, I Pe 4:3, II Pe 2:2, 7, 18, Ju 4.†
SYN.: ἀσωτία, profligacy, prodigality (v. Tr., Syn., § xvi; DB, iii, 46).

ἀσφαλῶς.as:
ἀσφαλῶς,
adv.,
[in LXX: Ge 34:25 (בֶּטַח), To 6:4, Wi 18:6, Ba 5:7, I Mac 6:40, III Mac 7:6*;]
(a)safely: Mk 14:44, Ac 16:23;
(b)assuredly: Ac 2:36.†

ἀσφάλεια.as:
ἀσφάλεια, -ας, ἡ
(< ἀσφαλής), [in LXX for בֶּטַח, etc.;]
1.firmness.
2.certainty: Lk 1:4.
3.security: Ac 5:23, I Th 5:3. (In π. it is used as a law-term, proof, security; v. MM, s.v.; M, I Th 5:3.)†

Ἀσήρ.long: Asher, one of the sons of Jacob, and founder of one of the Twelve Tribes.

ἀσώτως.der: adverb from the same as G810 (ἀσωτία);
ἀσώτως.as:
* ἀσώτως,
adv.
(< ἄσωτος, prodigal, wasteful), [in LXX for סרר, Pr 7:11*;]
wastefully: Lk 15:13 (EV, in riotous living; but not necessarily dissolute; cf. MM, ut supr.; Milligan, NTD, 79).†

ἀστράπτω.long: I flash (with, then like, lightning), am lustrous.
ἀστράπτω.as:
ἀστράπτω,
[in LXX for בּרק;]
to lighten, flash forth: Lk 17:2424:4 (MM, s.v.).†

ἄστρον.sd: properly, a constellation; put for a single star (natural or artificial)
ἄστρον.as:
ἄστρον, -ου, τό,
[in LXX chiefly for כּוֹכָב;]
(a) mostly in pl. (as in cl.), the stars: Lk 21:25, Ac 27:20, He 11:12;
(b) in sing. (Xen., al.), only of some noted star; the symbol or image of a star, Ac 7:43 (cf. ἀστήρ, and v. MM, s.v.).†

Ἀσία.g: roughly the western third of Asia Minor
Ἀσία.long: the Roman province of Asia, roughly the western third of Asia Minor.
Ἀσία.sd: Asia, i.e. Asia Minor, or (usually) only its western shore
Ἀσία.as:
Ἀσία, -ας, ἡ,
Asia, the Roman province: Ac 2:96:916:619:1, 10, 22, 26 (M, Pr., 73), Ac 19:27Ac 20:4, 16, 1821:2724:1827:2, Ro 16:5, I Co 16:19, II Co 1:8, II Ti 1:15, I Pe 1:1, Re 1:4.†

ἀστεῖος.long: (lit: belonging to the city; then: witty, clever), elegant, pretty, fair, fine, beautiful.
ἀστεῖος.as:
ἀστεῖος, -ον
(< ἄστυ, a city), [in LXX: Ex 2:2 (טוֹב), Nu 22:32 (οὐκ ἀ.ירט), Jg 3:17 (בָּרִיא), Jth 11:23, Da LXX, Sus 7, II Mac 6:23*;]
1.of the town.
2. (Like Lat. urbanus),
(a)courteous,
(b)elegant (in π., of clothing, MM, s.v.), comely, fair (as in Ex 2:2), He 11:23, Ac 7:20.†

Ἀσιάρχης.long: an Asiarch, an official connected with the worship of Rome and the Emperor in the Roman province Asia.
Ἀσιάρχης.sd: an Asiarch or president of the public festivities in a city of Asia Minor
Ἀσιάρχης.as:
*† Ἀσιάρχης, -ου, ὁ,
an Asiarch, one of ten officers elected by the various cities in the province of Asia whose duty it was to celebrate at their own charges the public games and festivals: Ac 19:31 (Strab., Inscr.; DB, s.v.).†

Ἀσιανός.g: belonging to the Roman province Asia
Ἀσιανός.long: belonging to the Roman province Asia.
Ἀσιανός.sd: an Asian (i.e. Asiatic) or an inhabitant of Asia
Ἀσιανός.as:
Ἀσιανός, -ή, -όν,
Asian, of Asia, Asiatic; as subst., ὁ (οἱ) Ἀ.: Ac 20:4.†

Ἆσσος.long: Assos, a port of Mysia, in the Roman province Asia.
Ἆσσος.sd: Assus, a city of Asia MInor
Ἆσσος.as:
Ἄσσος, -ου
(also Ἀσσός, -οῦ), ἡ,
Assos, a city on the E. coast of Asia Minor: Ac 20:13, 14 (v.s. ἆσσον).†

ἀσμένως.der: adverb from a derivative of the base of G2237 (ἡδονή);
ἀσμένως.as:
** ἀσμένως,
adv.
(< ἥδομαι, to be glad), [in LXX: II Mac 4:1210:33, III Mac 3:155:21*;]
gladly: Ac 21:17.†

ἀσφαλής.long: (lit: unfailing), safe, reliable, trustworthy, certain, sure.
ἀσφαλής.der: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and sphallo (to "fail");
ἀσφαλής.as:
ἀσφαλής, -ές
(< ἀ- neg., σφάλλω, to trip up), [in LXX for אשׁר pu., etc.;]
certain, secure, safe: Ac 21:3422:3025:26, Phl 3:1, He 6:19 (MM, s.v.).†

ἄσημος.der: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and the base of G4591 (σημαίνω);
ἄσημος.as:
ἄσημος, -ον
(< σῆμα, a mark), [in LXX: Ge 30:42 (עטף), Jb 42:11, III Mac 1:3*;]
without mark (in π. of an uncircumcised boy: Deiss., BS, 153; MM, s.v.). Metaph. (MM, s.v.), unknown, obscure: litotes, οὐκ ἄ (Eur., al.), πόλις, Ac 21:39.†

ἀσκέω.sd: to elaborate, i.e. (figuratively) train (by implication, strive)
ἀσκέω.der: probably from the same as G4632 (σκεῦος);
ἀσκέω.as:
** ἀσκέω, -ῶ,
[in LXX: II Mac 15:4*;]
1.to adorn (poët.).
2.to practise, exercise (Hdt., Xen.).
3.to endeavour (Xen., al.): c. inf., Ac 24:16.†

ἆσσον.der: neuter comparative of the base of G1451 (ἐγγύς);
ἆσσον.as:
* ἆσσον (Rec., after Vg., Ἄσσον),
adv. (compar. of ἄγχι, near),
nearer: Ac 27:13 (RV, close in shore; v. Bl., § 11, 3; 44, 3; poets, Ion, and late prose).†

ἀσιτία.long: either: lack or wheat, lack of food (the literal meaning), or: abstinence from food, a fast, loss of appetite, sea-sickness (the extended meaning).
ἀσιτία.as:
* ἀσιτία, -ας, ἡ
(< ἄσιτος),
fasting, abstinence from food: Ac 27:21.†
SYN.: νηστεία (MM, ut infr.).

ἄσιτος.der: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and G4621 (σῖτος);
ἄσιτος.as:
* ἄσιτος, -ον
(< ἀ- neg., σῖτος),
fasting, without eating (cf. MM, s.v.): Ac 27:33.†

ἀσάλευτος.der: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a derivative of G4531 (σαλεύω);
ἀσάλευτος.as:
ἀ-σάλευτος, -ον
(< σαλεύω), [in LXX: Ex 13:16, De 6:811:18 (טוֹטָפָוֹת)*;]
unmoved, immovable: Ac 27:41; metaph., He 12:28.†

ἀσύμφωνος.der: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and G4859 (σύμφωνος);
ἀσύμφωνος.as:
** ἀ-σύμφωνος, -ον,
[in LXX: Wi 18:10, Da, LXX, Bel 15*;]
dissonant, discordant; metaph., at variance: πρὸς ἀλλήλους, Ac 28:25.†

ἀσέβεια.as:
ἀσέβεια, -ας, ἡ
(< ἀσεβής), [in LXX for פֶּשַׁע, רֶשַׁע, etc.;]
ungodliness, impiety: Ro 1:1811:26, II Ti 2:16, Tit 2:12; ἔργα ἀσεβείας, ungodly deeds, Ju 15; ἐπιθυηίαι τ. ἀσεβειῶν, desires for ungodly things or deeds, Ju 18 (DB, iv, 532; Cremer, 523; MM, s.v.).†

ἀσχημοσύνη.long: unseemly behavior, unseemliness, indecency, shame, nakedness, an indecent (lewd) act.
ἀσχημοσύνη.sd: an indecency; by implication, the pudenda
ἀσχημοσύνη.as:
ἀσχημοσύνη, -ης, ἡ
(< ἀσχήμων), [in LXX chiefly for עֶרְוָה;]
unseemliness: Ro 1:27 (MM, s.v.); euphemism for ἡ αἰσχύνη, as freq. in LXX, shame, nakedness: Re 16:15.†

ἀσύνθετος.long: not covenanting, untrue to an agreement, treacherous.
ἀσύνθετος.sd: properly, not agreed, i.e. treacherous to compacts
ἀσύνθετος.der: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a derivative of G4934 (συντίθεμαι);
ἀσύνθετος.as:
ἀ-σύν-θετος, -ον
(< συντίθεμαι; v. M, Pr., 222; MM, s.v.), [in LXX: Je 3:7, 8, 10, 11 (בּגד)*;]
false to engagements, not keeping covenant, faithless (MM, s.v.): Ro 1:31.†

ἄστοργος.der: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of (to cherish affectionately);
ἄστοργος.as:
* ἄστοργος, -ον
(< στοργή, family affection, love of kindred, v.s. ἀγάπη),
without natural affection: Ro 1:31, II Ti 3:3 (MM, s.v.).†

ἀσπίς.sd: a buckler (or round shield); used of a serpent (as coiling itself), probably the "asp"
ἀσπίς.as:
ἀσπίς, -ίδος, ἡ,
[in LXX for פֶּתֶן, etc.;]
an asp: Ro 3:13.†

ἀσεβής.sd: irreverent, i.e. (by extension) impious or wicked
ἀσεβής.der: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of G4576 (σέβομαι);
ἀσεβής.as:
ἀσεβής, -ές
(σέβω, to reverence), [in LXX chiefly for רשׁע;]
ungodly, impious: Ro 4:55:6, I Ti 1:9, I Pe 4:18, II Pe 2:5, 63:7, Ju 4, 15.†

ἀσθένημα.as:
* ἀσθένημα, -τος, τό
(< ἀσθενής),
an infirmity (MM, s.v.): Ro 15:1.†

Ἀσύγκριτος.der: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a derivative of G4793 (συγκρίνω);

ἀστατέω.g: I am unsettled, have no fixed abode
ἀστατέω.long: I am unsettled, have no fixed abode, lead a vagabond life.
ἀστατέω.der: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a derivative of G2476 (ἵστημι);
ἀστατέω.as:
**† ἀστατέω, -ῶ
(< ἄστατος, unstable), [in Aq.: Is 58:7 (LXX, ἄστεγος)*;]
to be unsettled, be homeless, lead a vagabond life (Cremer, 738 MM, s.v.): I Co 4:11.†

ἀσχημονέω.long: I act improperly, am unseemly, behave unbecomingly (or even dishonorably); perhaps: I consider (something) unseemly.
ἀσχημονέω.as:
ἀσχημονέω, -ῶ
(< ἀσχήμαων), [in LXX: Ez 16:7, 22, 3923:29 (עֶרְיָה); De 25:3 (קלה ni.)*;]
to act unbecomingly, behave dishonourably: I Co 13:5; seq. ἐπί, I Co 7:36 (MM, s.v.).†

ἀσχήμων.der: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of G2192 (ἔχω) (in the sense of its congener G4976 (σχῆμα));
ἀσχήμων.as:
ἀσχήμων, -ον
(< ἀ- neg., σχῆμα), [in LXX: Ge 34:7 (נְבָלָה), De 24:1 (עֶרְוָה), Wi 2:20, Da TH Sus 63, II Mac 9:2*;]
1.shapeless.
2.uncomely, unseemly: I Co 12:23.†

ἄσοφος.der: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and G4680 (σοφός);
ἄσοφος.as:
ἄ-σοφος, -ον,
[in LXX: Pr 9:8א2 A*;]
unwise, foolish: Eph 5:15.†

ἀσωτία.der: from a compound of G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of G4982 (σώζω);
ἀσωτία.as:
ἀσωτία, -ας, ἡ
(< ἀ- neg., σώζω), [in LXX: Pr 28:7 (זלל), II Mac 6:4*;]
prodigality, wastefulness, profligacy: Eph 5:18, Tit 1:6, I Pe 4:4 (MM, s.v.).†
SYN.: ἀσέλγεια, q.v.

ἀστοχέω.g: I miss the mark, miss my aim, make a false aim
ἀστοχέω.long: I miss the mark, miss my aim, make a false aim, fail.
ἀστοχέω.sd: to miss the mark, i.e. (figuratively) deviate from truth
ἀστοχέω.der: from a compound of G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and (an aim);
ἀστοχέω.as:
**† ἀστοχέω, -ῶ
(στόχος, a mark), [in LXX: Si 7:198:9*;]
to miss the mark, fail: c. gen., I Ti 1:6 (so in π., MM, s.v.); seq. περί, I Ti 6:21, II Ti 2:18.†

ἄσπιλος.der: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and G4695 (σπιλόω);
ἄσπιλος.as:
**† ἄ-σπιλος, -ον
(< ἀ- neg., σπῖλος), [in Sm.: Jb 15:15 (LXX, καθαρός)*;]
spotless, unstained: I Pe 1:19; metaph., I Ti 6:14, Ja 1:27, II Pe 3:14 (for exx., v. MM, s.v.).†
SYN.: ἀμίαντος, ἄμωμος.

ἄσπονδος.long: implacable, "not to be bound by truce".
ἄσπονδος.sd: literally, without libation (which usually accompanied a treaty), i.e. (by implication) truceless
ἄσπονδος.der: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a derivative of G4689 (σπένδω);
ἄσπονδος.as:
* ἄσπονδος, -ον
(< σπονδή, a libation);
1.without truce (Thuc.).
2.admitting of no truce, implacable (Dem., al.): II Ti 3:3.†

ἀστήρικτος.der: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of G4741 (στηρίζω);

ἀσεβέω.g: I am impious, irreverent, do impiously
ἀσεβέω.sd: to be (by implied act) impious or wicked
ἀσεβέω.kj: commit (live, that after should live) ungodly
ἀσεβέω.as:
ἀσεβέω, -ῶ
(< ἀσεβής), [in LXX for פּשׁע, רשׁע;]
to be ungodly, act profanely: II Pe 2:6; c. cogn. acc. (MM, s.v.), Ju 15.†
